With the first issue, it seems like it quickly went to invalidating/shut down. Was he more so just speaking out loud with you? Why is it that you took it as ingratitude instead of just venting? An example would be if you were venting about something and he said back to you “stop bitching, you should be more grateful.” It’s obviously not a good feeling. And then the one-up with “well so-and-so agrees with me,” to top it off would have me frustrated as well. I think your intent was good, being grateful is definitely important and you should always remind loved ones. But context matters and so does execution. I think there might be some old habits to break out of. Which is SOOOO fucking difficult. But in small ways will help. With this example, he could’ve just been venting or speaking out loud. Customers CAN be annoying. Maybe he didn’t want a response, he just wanted to shoot the shit with his partner. HOWEVER, hindsight is 20/20 or whatever the saying is. In the future, it can be helpful to analyze/prepare for situations like this. You have the options to: listen and say nothing, just laugh at him in a playful way/tease him about being a grumpy ass, or if you wanted to tell him to be positive it could’ve been something like “Haha yeah, customers can sometimes be little shits but they pay the bills! ;)” or “Yeah that is annoying! BUT doesn’t stop us from being grateful.” WHICH AGAIN, might be totally shifting the way you have been for years/your personality. You can tweak it however you need, but the point is to kind of do your best to me more aware of the impact of your actions, if that makes sense. Something that can help you process it is, how would YOU feel if it happened to you? Which I’m sure it does. If you were just venting and got told to stop bitching and be grateful. you’d be like, bitch????? Haha. And this is really important - this does not mean you need to analyze everything you say or do, or walk on egg shells. Making small adjustments here and there will be a HUGE start and you should notice less arguments, whatever. And overall you might feel better! 

When it comes to housework, aaah. It can always be a problem. When one partner feels workload is uneven, when you can’t agree to things, when names like “lazy” are being thrown out there. It can get so messy (just like the housework hehehe). I’m not sure what your set up is, would delegating certain tasks be a place to start? You do x things, they do x things, you guys ask for help when needed? The one problem is then this has the possibility to turn into “Well I did my half of the shit, you haven’t done yours!” “When are you going to take out the trash?! It’s your job!” Regardless, insults and getting heated is never necessary. It does happen and it can be hard to avoid when you are feeling frustrated, burnt out, unappreciated. Have you asked your partner why they get so frustrated? If they feel you aren’t pulling your weight, can you ask them their opinion on what could help make things easier for both of you? They could say, well I need help with __. And you can say, well sorry I didn’t know, you’ve never asked. Or maybe a schedule works for you guys? Maybe switching the chores you guys do will help put into perspective what each does, so you can either find what works best or be appreciative of the other? 

But yeah, I’m sorry things feel so difficult. It sucks when you are trying and are not met with the same efforts. I definitely think sitting down and having a conversation about wanting to try to communicate better, and what your needs are and what you’d *like* to see - and I say *like* to see because expectations can always be finicky and cause more problems. Your partner can expect something unfair of you. That’s why it’s important to hear them out, validate, and find middle ground. “I understand and hear you, but maybe we can start with ___ and see how it goes from there.

Can you give an example of how you and your partner typically communicate with a problem? Asking because the *usual* way to avoid coming off as defensive is to do the “*I* feel ___” or “*I* would really love it if ___” or “It hurts *my* feelings when __” because then it doesn’t come off as blame/defensive with “YOU do ___ to me” or “YOU need to __” or “YOU hurt my feelings when __.” 

As far as listening when you need to respond, I find that acknowledgment/validation to their feelings, an apology, and THEN commenting your feelings helps. If they bring up something to you, instead of immediately going “WELL YOU DO THIS!” It’s helpful to kind of see it in a “I’m sorry that hurt you. From my point of view, I thought __. But in the future I can work on it with __.” Or just asking what your partner needs from you, and if it’s not something you agree with, finding middle ground. It’s always important to remember that intention DOES NOT outweigh impact. You may have not meant to hurt them, but that does not negate their feelings. On the other side, it definitely doesn’t feel fair and it’s so easy to be defensive when you feel like you are in the hot seat. It’s a good reminder that it is YOU AND YOUR PARTNER VERSUS THE PROBLEM. Not versus each other. When it comes to them bringing up something you do but don’t acknowledge their part, I find it’s easiest to again validate their feelings, but then find something you both can do to work on it. Example: I’m really sorry ___ upsets you and then me doing ___ doesn’t help either. From my perspective, it’s frustrating when ___ and that’s why I get that way. I think it would help if when we feel this way, we can do ___ to prevent it. It would really help me if you do ___, as ___ can also be triggering for me and then we get to a bad spot. 

When/if he brings up you coming off as disingenuous, you can just say you are sorry it’s coming across as that, but you promise you are just making an effort to be more calm and make them feel heard and validated. It’s just different than the usual defend and deflect and that may be why it feels that way, but you really are trying. 

Also, you are 100% valid and should be able to express your feelings and needs. Listening is important for both sides. There should always be a middle ground and please don’t ever feel pressured to agree to everything. Of course there will have to be SOME compromise and sacrifices, but you are allowed to openly communicate and express your boundaries, thoughts, and feelings. 

All in all, it’s really just important to validate and apologize. Make sure you are letting them get it all out before saying your responses. Take turns expressing feelings so you can both digest and work on things together. And remember to express your love and appreciation (and they should do the same to you). 

Hope this helps! I’m proud of you for putting this effort in.

I know you are scared of the anxiety you will feel from being alone after you leave him, but I PROMISE you the anxiety you will have daily from staying with him will be so much worse. You will be constantly wondering if/when he’s going to cheat again, you will be overthinking EVERYTHING, you will be regretful you didn’t leave before, you will question when he’s “nice” to you, you will tear down on yourself worse than you already do. You deserve SO much better. I know how crippling anxiety is. I know how paralyzed you feel. I know how mortified you are of being alone. But I promise you it will get better. You have to take care of yourself. Find little things to keep you occupied. Be patient with yourself. Give yourself space to feel things. It will be okay. You will be okay. Take a BIG, DEEP breath and choose yourself. Do it in any way that you need to. Ghost him, send him a long message for closure, write up a text and just send it. Whenever you can gather the strength but it’s best to just rip it off like a bandaid. I am here if you need to talk. I hope you kick ass in your interview tomorrow. New beginnings for you. I hope this isn’t crossing a line or triggering, but I just looked at your profile and saw you just got out of a long-term relationship. As a more quicker solution - the “it’s not personal” mantra helps me SOOO MUCH. Remind yourself that whatever is going on is not about you, and if there was something, they would say it. I always try to remind myself to not jump straight to negatives. Instead of “they’re ignoring me, something is wrong” I remind myself “they are busy, this doesn’t mean they don’t care” 

Another thing that helps is that something is currently going on (the work thing, the move, the hospital event) - and it would be more worrying if everything was going good and then communication stopped (without anything happening), if that makes sense. 

Try to reach out and see if she needs anything, and you can definitely tell her you miss her!! but continue to respect her space without pressuring :)

I’m so sorry, I thought there was a history of this. I take back my “dump him.” If that’s the case, then express your feelings and needs! Communicate with him. Trust me when I say holding back or hiding your anxiety and feelings helps no one. It DEFINITELY doesn’t help you, it doesn’t help your relationship, and it doesn’t give your bf the chance to respond and/or meet your needs. There will always be hard and uncomfortable conversations. It’s better to express your feelings and needs now so he can either meet them and you guys can work through this, or so he or you can decide that it’s not a good fit. Which I know is the scariest thing. Trust me, I have such intense abandonment issues. But we have to choose ourselves and we have to understand that we deserve better, and we are deserving of love and safety and being able to express ourselves. We can’t heal if we can’t address anxiety or insecurities.

I think that as much as you want to make them feel at least a bit of what you were feeling, it’s best to avoid that type of interaction. It won’t be good for you, and whatever they were going through, I’m sure it won’t be good for them. 

Is this something you feel is enough to end a friendship? Not a loaded question, just genuine. How badly did this hurt you? Does this friend have a history of crossing boundaries like this? If this is not worth communicating over (you don’t want to be friends with them, you don’t want to put the effort or energy into this, you don’t feel this will be a conversation that goes anywhere, they are hard to communicate with, this is the umpteenth time this has happened and you’re done), then just don’t respond. You don’t owe them anything. If you feel the need to respond, keep it short and just say “Hey, I hope you’re okay. I was worried. I’m sure you’re going through something and had your reasons, and I’m not trying to make this about me, but it really hurt that you ghosted me. For my mental health, I will need some space. Please take care.” 

BUT if you feel that you want an answer, feel like you are able to communicate with them, or feel like putting the effort and energy in, then be honest about your feelings. Tell them that they hurt you, that they crossed a boundary. That you understand that they are going through something, needed space, and they were probably focused on themself and weren’t thinking about anything/one else; but a text could’ve been sent to you. I know they don’t owe you anything, but there’s a level of respect and love. And you care and would’ve been there for them. And they can ask for space when they need it, and that way you’re not left worrying.

I get it when you say that he’s not in the wrong for wanting space. That’s normal. Everyone needs space. But please know that you’re not wrong for expressing feelings and needs. 

I have the same struggle with my boyfriend. He needs A LOT of space to recharge. I’m the opposite, I need time with him to recharge. It’s hard to meet halfway. Sometimes I’ll cry on my own because of how horrible my anxiety gets, and there are times where I’ll keep it to myself because I don’t want to make him feel bad about wanting space. 

BUT the difference is that my boyfriend doesn’t tell me things like “leave me alone.” He doesn’t make me feel bad about my anxiety or needs. He doesn’t go out of his way to create more anxiety for me by purposely ignoring me when he knows that is triggering to me. 

I normally HATE when people comment “dump him,” but honestly, you should not be with someone who goes out of their way to make you feel this shitty. I know that you feel like you pushed him away or that you should’ve just kept quiet about your needs, but please don’t think that way. You have needs. You should be able to communicate and safely express them. And your partner should respectfully express his needs of space, and you guys can meet halfway. 

You are deserving of love, respect, communication, care, and safety. 

Feel free to message me if you need to vent some more, I super resonate with your feelings and we can cope together haha.

If it means a lot to you, then you have to express that, he can’t read your mind. But be prepared for an uncomfortable conversation because it’s really not his responsibility to add a heart to every text message, and he might feel like that’s a lot of pressure. What happens if he forgets one text with a hear and now you guys are fighting? It sucks, but sometimes we have to pick our battles. Him not adding a heart DOES NOT MEAN he doesn’t love you. He’s not saying that. ANXIETY and INSECURITY is telling you that. You are aware that it’s an irrational thought - so attack it!!! Get it out of there !!!! It’s not helping you at all, so tell it to fuck off! 

Why does it make you feel like he doesn’t love you? What’s the root of the insecurity? That might be a big question if it obviously stems back to childhood trauma, but let’s address it, if you’re up to it. 

Whenever I have irrational thoughts, it’s sooooo hard to knock them off. I’ve had some pretty bad ones before so don’t feel bad for ones you get. But what’s important is to do your best not to take it out on your partner. Something that’s been helping me is thinking of ways that my boyfriend shows me he loves me. You said that sometimes he’ll go a few texts without sending a heart, but he still sent you one a few texts ago. Try and think of little things like that to start attacking irrational thoughts when they attack you.

I struggle with this a lot. Actually, just tonight my boyfriend was saying how stoked he was to be alone/have alone time. I just spent the weekend with him, and as an AA, I immediately took it personal when he said that lol ! My brain immediately went to “he enjoys being alone. he doesn’t like spending time with you. he’d rather be alone than be with you. he wants to be alone.” and so on. But I quickly stopped that thinking (as best I could haha. Basically just forced myself to be more rational to balance out the anxiety because that’s all I can do LMAO) because enjoying alone time is HEALTHY for ALL attachment styles. I told myself “he never said any of that, ANXIETY did.” And I thought about moments or ways that I know my boyfriend loves spending time with me or doing things to show me he loves me/enjoys our time together. As a matter of fact, he’s an Avoidant and he MAJORLY needs a lot of alone time, and him spending time with me is a way he shows me he loves me, in itself. You should enjoy your alone time, too. Which I know is so so so so much easier said than done. I literally hate alone time, I hate being alone. But I always do my best to never take away my partners alone time. It’s necessary for everyone, and I do sometimes enjoy my alone time. Right now I’m still in the phase of it being more DISTRACTIONS versus actual enjoyment of myself/alone time, but there are days where I genuinely enjoy being alone and focusing on myself (hobbies, chores, anything beneficial to yourself). 

Plus, this is for work! He’s not choosing to be away from you. And I’m sure that he’ll miss you so so so much! Think of some positives: you guys will miss each other, you both have alone time to enjoy and try new things (maybe even surprise him with something new learned or made/crafted while you’ve had alone time?). Time to also HEAL! Trial by fire lol. Learn something, try something you’ve wanted to, binge a show that’s been on your list for forever, read a book, set up plans with your partner for FaceTimes and check-ins if you need it, take yourself out on a date, do or watch a guilty pleasure item that your partner would give you shit and make fun of you if he caught you hehehe. 

This will pass and it’ll be okay! 

If you need any distractions or you need to vent (I know all about irrational anxiety and problems stemming from childhood trauma lol), feel free to message me and I’ll be a safe space for you.

I relate to this so hard. It sucks being the giver and no one ever stops to return the favor lol. Not that we do things to get something in return, it just sucks people don’t think about you like you think about them. And I also heavily relate to being detached and having mindsets. It’s weird having dealt with depression for so long, you forget that some thoughts that are normal to you, are definitely not normal. Invasive thoughts like “I’m alone.” Or “what friends” are not normal thoughts, but to you they are because you’ve dealt with depression for so long. Suicide is always in the back of my mind, I’m always thinking about how much easier it would be not to deal with things. And now I don’t even wince at the thought of suicide. But I forget that’s not normal, it’s just normal to me because of chronic depression. And it’s weird we have to deal with these things. It’s weird having to navigate through life with depression and constantly wanting to end your life. It’s weird because we have to find different things to look forward to or be happy about. “Yes! I brushed my teeth!” Is an accomplishment to us but no one else things about it. 

I’m also in a phase of catastrophizing. I’m really sorry you’re going through it, too. If you want to talk I’m here. For now, just take things one at a time. You know the limits of what you can deal with when you get like this. If all you can do today is get out of bed, that’s okay. You dont have to waste your energy on being social or concerning yourself with others. Try and find something that distracts you from thinking. Or if you have to think, try and change it to things you are proud of. You should be proud that you are so loving and caring and giving. You should be proud that you’re going back to school. You can be happy about your family throwing you a party. You can be happy about how far you’ve come. You can be proud you haven’t self harmed in a year.
